prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1474; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the policyholder's vehicle occupant reporting a low-speed head-on collision with another vehicle. Claim opened and assigned for review.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of the reported loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant by phone. The account of the collision was clear and matched the initial report in its sequence and details.

Entry 4: Reviewed the photographs submitted with the claim. They confirm several key details of the scene and the position of both vehicles, though no independent witnesses have come forward.

Entry 5: Police report obtained. It confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision, and the responding officer's notes are consistent with the photographs.

Entry 6: Inspected the vehicle damage. The damage pattern lines up with the described impact and the reported speed range, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspection records.

Entry 7: Claimant reported neck pain and stiffness consistent with whiplash. The reported symptoms fit the kind and force of the crash well.

Entry 8: Medical records received from the treating provider. No prior injury to the same body area is recorded in the claimant's history or in available prior claims data.

Entry 9: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this injury. Requested updated treatment notes and a treatment plan to understand the recovery timeline.

Entry 10: Claimant was re-contacted for a follow-up interview. The account of events was the same as in every previous conversation, with no material differences in the timeline or description.

Entry 11: File reviewed and all documentation is in order. Recommend moving the injury component to evaluation for settlement, pending receipt of the updated treatment notes.
